articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino agrees deal to stay as US coach through World Cup 2030
articles.excerpt: Pochettino joined US national team in 2024 Coach led US to last 16 at 2026 World Cup US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino and the US Soccer Federation…
articles.body: Pochettino joined US national team in 2024 Coach led US to last 16 at 2026 World Cup US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino and the US Soccer Federation have agreed to a contract extension that will keep Pochettino attached to the program through 2030, US Soccer announced on Monday. The two sides had been actively engaged in discussions on a contract extension for several months, long before the USMNT’s disappointing, last-16 exit in this summer’s World Cup, with the federation making it clear it desired Pochettino to stay. Conversations picked up in the weeks following the World Cup, with the Guardian reporting last week that the sides had been in the “final stages” of agreeing to a deal. Financial details of the contract extension were not released, but Pochettino is expected to get a raise on top of the $6m per year he earned under his previous deal with the federation – already the largest outlay for a US head coach. articles.title: ‘They are terrified’: Como spark row with fans over controversial new stadium policy
articles.excerpt: Supporters must not miss more than three home games Serie A club’s chairman defends harsh new rules The surprise package of last season’s Serie A, Como, who qualified…
articles.body: Supporters must not miss more than three home games Serie A club’s chairman defends harsh new rules The surprise package of last season’s Serie A, Como, who qualified for the Champions League for the first time in the club’s history , will revoke season tickets from fans who fail to attend four home matches, under a series of new rules that have sparked a row among supporters. In a statement issued on Monday the club, coached by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas , said its supporters “who miss more than three home matches without what it considers a valid reason risk having their season tickets revoked”. Another new rule bans fans from wearing the opposing team’s shirts or scarves anywhere in the stadium except the away section. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘It’s my time’: Christos Tzolis fighting fit for Arsenal on return to England
articles.excerpt: The £34m signing from Club Brugge says he is a more complete player now after an indifferent time at Norwich For any Arsenal fan eager to know what Christos Tzolis might…
articles.body: The £34m signing from Club Brugge says he is a more complete player now after an indifferent time at Norwich For any Arsenal fan eager to know what Christos Tzolis might bring to the Premier League champions, the winger’s swiftly earned nickname at his new club might prove instructive. In the 2006 action film 300 , the leading figure of King Leonidas guides a meagre bunch of Spartans against an overwhelmingly large invading army. Although doomed by the vast numerical disadvantage, Leonidas’s courage, determination and strength inspires his troops far beyond their means. It is his name that Arsenal’s fitness coaches have given their new Greek. Within a week of his £34m move from Club Brugge , Tzolis had made himself conspicuous at Arsenal’s training ground by acing a host of pre-season tests, topping the charts in one particular fitness challenge that involves players running more than a kilometre over varying intervals. Modesty forbids him from revealing the remainder of his physical results but, with a smile, he concedes they were “good”. Continue reading...

articles.title: English FA to drop support for Gianni Infantino after Wales withdraw backing
articles.excerpt: FAW says Fifa president has lost its confidence Pressure continues to build after doomed World Cup plan The Football Association will formally withdraw its support for…
articles.body: FAW says Fifa president has lost its confidence Pressure continues to build after doomed World Cup plan The Football Association will formally withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s re-election as the Fifa president, adding to the mounting pressure on his crisis-hit tenure. In a significant development, the FA will write to Fifa confirming it no longer backs Infantino for a fourth term in charge, having previously offered its endorsement. Their move comes after the Welsh FA dropped its backing for Infantino’s candidature. More European countries are expected to follow suit in an attempt to force his resignation. The Football Association of Finland became the first country to withdraw its support last week. Continue reading...
